subject:
Logging controls & PII redaction 














follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Logging controls & PII redaction — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alice / Bob - great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and the follow-ups we discussed so we’re aligned: 

1) Goals from your side
- Must retain request/response logs for debugging and traceability
- Cannot persist PII (PII = user names, emails, full SSNs, payment tokens) in plaintext
- Logs must be stored in US region and be configurable for retention

2) Controls Redwood can offer (high level)
- Configurable logging level per-route (none, minimal, full)
- Request/response redaction rules (regex-based + schema rules) before persistence
- Header scrubbing (Authorization, Cookie, X-Auth-Token)
- Option to remove or hash trace IDs before writing to disk if you only need correlation for short-term debugging
- Retention window configurable (e.g., 30 / 90 / 365 days) and automatic purging

3) Questions from our side to finalize a proposal
- Do you need request/response bodies for all routes or only for a subset (debugging vs analytics)?
- Preferred retention window (default / maximum)?
- Any required encryption/HSM requirements for log keys beyond our SOC2 controls?

Next steps: I’ve attached a short overview of our logging controls and a sample redaction spec. Can you confirm the answers to the three questions above and share any specific fields you want redacted by name? Happy to schedule a follow-up with our security engineer this week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-logging-controls-overview.pdf (overview), redwood-pii-redaction-spec.xlsx (sample rules)

From: Alice Ramos <alice.ramos@fintechco.com>

Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:28:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Logging controls & PII redaction — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa - good recap. A few clarifications from our security/privacy team: 

- We need request/response bodies for debugging for ~10% of traffic (sampled) and for specific error traces. We cannot keep full request payloads for more than 30 days unless redacted.
- Required PII redaction list: email addresses, full name, SSN, payment instrument numbers. Partial tokens (last4) are OK.
- Trace IDs: we use them for correlating across services. We need trace IDs to exist in logs for 7 days. After that they should be hashed/rotated or removed before long-term storage.
- Data residency: must be stored in the US (us-east) for now.
- Retention: goal is 90 days for most logs, 30 days for raw request bodies unless redacted.

Also: are headers (Authorization, Cookie) persisted in any form if we enable "full" logging? If so, can we have a per-header toggle to scrub them?

On the procurement side, pricing impact if we disable logging for sensitive routes vs keeping sampled logs would be good to understand.

Happy to jump on a short technical call with your security engineer - Wed/Thu this week works for our team.

- Alice Ramos
Head of Platform Security, FintechCo
alice.ramos@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ramos <alice.ramos@fintechco.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 13:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Logging controls & PII redaction — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Alice - that’s very helpful. Answers inline + next steps: 

- Sampling: we support sampling at the router level (percentage-based) and per-route sampling. We can set to ~10% for general traffic and 100% for flagged error routes.
- Redaction: our redaction engine supports both regex and schema-driven rules. Common patterns (emails, SSN, card numbers) are available out of the box. Customers can add custom rules or upload a spec (we reviewed the sample you sent).
- Trace IDs: we can keep trace IDs unmodified for the short window (configurable, default 7 days), after which they are hashed with a customer-scoped salt before longer-term storage - this preserves correlation for mid-term analysis while preventing raw correlation later. We also offer a mode that removes trace IDs entirely before persistence if you prefer.
- Headers: header scrubbing is configurable per-header (Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, X-User-Email, etc.). If you enable full logging we do NOT persist Authorization/Cookie by default unless explicitly toggled and approved in an intake.
- Retention: configurable per-customer and per-log-class. We can propose default tiers (30/90/365). Purge runs are automatic and auditable.
- Encryption & compliance: logs are encrypted at rest using AES-256. We integrate with customer-managed KMS for additional key control if needed. We are SOC2 Type II compliant and can share the report under NDA.

Attachments: I’ve attached our logging controls overview and a sample redaction spec (the same docs referenced earlier).

Recommended next steps:
- Schedule 30-minute technical session with our security engineer (we’re available Wed 01/13 10:00-12:00 PST or Thu 01/14 11:00-1:00 PST) - propose Wed 10:30 PST?
- I’ll loop in Priyom (cc’d) to provide a short pricing delta for sampled logging vs disabling logs on sensitive routes and for custom retention tiers.
- Share a list of specific fields you want redacted by name (if you have a data dictionary).

Priyom / Neha - can you prepare a quick pricing delta (ballpark) and note any contract language we should expect for retention/sidecar logging clauses?

Thanks,
Marissa
